summary: High-level walkthrough of Redwood Optimize console and cost runbook focused on prefetch/prefix KV cache + batching recommendations for Ridgefield's shipment-tracking LLM use case. Discussed tradeoffs between latency SLO and token cost, reserved capacity vs hosted burst, and security/compliance gating for a pilot. Agreed next steps: pricing scenarios, security docs, and a 1-week sandbox benchmark.
topics: cost model scenarios (per-token vs reserved GPU)
security: KMS, data residency, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um I'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Laura: Hi I'm Laura Diaz, Head of ML at Ridgefield. Samir's here too.
[00:12] Samir: hi all Samir Rao, platform.
[00:14] Priya: Priya Menon, CTO.
[00:16] Ethan: Ethan Cole, SRE.
[00:20] Owen: great thanks, i'll be walking through the Optimize console and the prefetch prefex — excuse me — prefix KV cache patterns and the cost scenarios. Just a quick agenda: 1) baseline of your traffic and goals, 2) how we think about prefetch/prefix cache and sessionization, 3) batching & concurrency knobs, 4) cost runbook and reserved vs hosted options, 5) Q&A + next steps.
[01:10] Laura: that sounds good, our main goal is stable 100ms 95th percentile for the tracking endpoint, and keep token costs under our current infra spend which is tight. Also we have to keep PII out of logs, and all keys go through our KMS.
[01:40] Owen: yeah good call, we'll show encryption at rest options and how the console surfaces KMS integrations. Quick question on request shapes: do you have many short single-turn queries or longer multi-turn sessions?
[02:05] Samir: mostly short, 8-12 tokens of user input but we do have follow-up clarifications, so session affinity matters — we want the KV cache to reduce costs for repeated lookups but not increase tail latency.
[02:30] Owen: perfect, that's where prefix cache and lookahead prefetch helps. I'll share my screen. (screen share)
[03:05] [03:05] Owen: here's the Optimize console, the savings simulator, you can plug in qps, avg tokens, session hit rates. note: console auto-suggest sometimes shows "Redwood Optima" in older builds — UI bug, ignore that.
[03:45] Owen: baseline scenario A: no cache, 100 qps, avg 35 tokens per response, cost is X. Scenario B: prefix KV cache with 40% hit rate drops token cost by ~28% in our model. Scenario C: add prefetch lookahead (sessionization 80%) adds another 12% token savings but increases memory and a small chance of stale KV if TTL is short.
[05:10] Priya: can you expand on stale concerns? we have frequent updates to shipment ETA, cache staleness could be a problem.
[05:25] Owen: sure, TTL strategy is key — for ETA we recommend short TTL with validation-on-miss. prefetch is best for stable context like customer profile or static routing info. For rapidly changing ETA, you can do a two-tier: prefix cache for stable context, and per-request fetch for volatile fields.
[06:05] Ethan: network-wise we are VPC-only, strict egress, and our KMS is on-prem HSM. How does Redwood Private fit?
[06:22] Lena: we have a Private deployment option that keeps the control plane in a customer VPC and supports bring-your-own-KMS. There are a few packaging permutations for air-gapped or HSM integrations.
[06:50] Laura: great. What about reserved capacity vs hosted? We want cost predictability but not overcommit.
[07:05] Owen: reserved (Dedicated) gives you predictable throughput and a lower per-token compute cost at commit. Hosted API is flexible and easier for spikes. Our cost model in the console can show a 6-month commit curve: at your target throughput, 20% saving vs on-demand for a 3-month commit, ~32% for 12-month. We'll include scenarios in the pricing doc.
[08:00] Samir: curious on batching: our latency SLO is strict, how much batching can we tolerate?
[08:18] Owen: batching trades latency for cost; with continuous batching and our HTB scheduler, small micro-batches (~4-8) can preserve p95 close to no-batch if you keep priority lanes for low-latency traffic. For your 100ms p95, we recommend concurrency tuning and dynamic burst lanes rather than large batch sizes.
[09:05] Maya: i'll note that we ran a similar workload for a marketplace customer and kept p95 within 10% of baseline with hybrid lanes.
[09:30] Priya: any concerns about model routing? we may want cheaper quantized variants for non-critical responses.
[09:45] Owen: yep, console supports model variant routing with automatic fallback. e.g., primary high-precision model, fallback to quantized 4-bit for less-sensitive paths. Cost simulation accounts for variant mix.
[10:20] [10:20] Owen: jumping back to cache math — here's the simulator where I enter your numbers: 100 qps, 40% session hit assumed, avg output tokens 35, prefix cache reduces avg tokens served per request from 35 to 21. With prefetch (lookahead) and 70% session hit, tokens further drop to 14. This results in a per-month delta of about $8.7k in compute cost in our spreadsheet, depending on reserved vs on-demand.
[12:00] Laura: that $8.7k assumes what model family?
[12:08] Owen: good call — the baseline was a 13B open model quantized to 4-bit; if you use a larger 70B model numbers change, but the percentage savings from cache is similar.
[12:30] Samir: ok, how do we instrument to trust hit rates?
[12:40] Owen: console exposes token-level breakdowns and cache hit metrics. we'll also provide trace hooks you can pump into your telemetry for independent validation.
[13:10] Ethan: any PII leakage risk through prefix cache? we need to ensure logs don't store user PII and cached entries are encrypted.
[13:25] Lena: cached entries in our Private offering can be encrypted with your KMS keys; and audit logs can be configured to redact payloads. We'll share the security pack that details encryption, TTL, and log retention policies.
[14:00] Maya: i want to call out a tradeoff: aggressive prefetch increases memory usage and possible cost on GPU memory, so our savings calculator includes a memory/instance cost line item — sometimes the net saving is smaller if you need larger instance classes.
[14:40] Priya: do you support hybrid cache (some prefix keys in memory, rest in redis)?
[14:50] Owen: yes, our runtime supports both in-process KV and remote backing store. For low-latency hot hits we keep in-process; for less frequently-accessed keys we fall back to Redis or customer-managed store.
[15:25] Samir: performance question — at 500 rps, what's the expected p95 with a small-batch strategy?
[15:40] Owen: it depends on request size, but for your token sizes with continuous batching and priority lanes, p95 usually remains under 130ms at 500 rps on a Dedicated pool sized per our right-sizing tool. We'll validate in the sandbox.
[16:10] Laura: ok how does billing work for cache hits? we only want to pay for generated tokens not for cache reads.
[16:25] Maya: cache reads are cheap — we bill based on generated tokens and the instance runtime; cache hit reduces generated tokens so you see savings on token billing line item. We'll surface a detailed breakdown in the invoice preview.
[17:00] Owen: quick demo of the sandbox provisioning flow. (narrates steps) Note: some of the UI labels still say "prefetch simulator beta" — the build we use for customers is slightly different.
[18:20] [18:20] Owen: demo, provisioning: select model, choose Dedicated or Hosted, toggle prefix cache, set TTL, choose lookahead window, set sessionization keys (we recommend userID + deviceID). Then run the savings sim.
[20:10] Priya: what's the expected lead time for a dedicated pool?
[20:20] Lena: depends on region and commit; typically 2-4 weeks for Dedicated capacity with a small rolling window for reserved. For Private on-prem there's an onboarding cadence of 4-8 weeks depending on network and HSM setup.
[21:00] Samir: do we need to change our request shapes? we currently send a single fused payload with a ton of context.
[21:10] Owen: you can keep it but prefix cache works best when we can identify stable prefixes (like customer profile, last known ETA) separately. If you can split those into structured fields we can cache them and reduce token churn.
[22:00] Laura: what's the failure mode if cache store is down?
[22:10] Owen: runtime falls back to fetch-on-miss; there's a small latency spike but the system is designed to degrade gracefully. we also have automatic fallback to a compatible quantized model if capacity is strained.
[22:45] Ethan: about audit logs — we need immutable logs for compliance for 12 months.
[22:55] Lena: we support configurable retention and export to your S3 or SIEM; with Private we can integrate with your existing WORM storage as well.
[23:25] Maya: ok to pivot to pricing caveats: commit levels, minimums, and overage.
[23:35] Maya: reserved is a commit, you'll get lower per-hour instance price; overages billed at on-demand. There's also an SLA tier with 99.95% uptime for Dedicated.
[24:00] Priya: can we do a pilot with a soft commit? like a 3-month with opt-out?
[24:10] Maya: yes we do flexible pilots; we'll model a 3-month pilot with a cap and convertible credits if you convert to a 12-month.
[24:35] Samir: let's talk about the bench plan you mentioned earlier.
[24:40] Owen: plan: 1) provision sandbox (Dedicated scaled to expected throughput), 2) replay your traces at 100/250/500 rps, 3) measure p50/p95/p99, model hit-rates and token-costs, 4) iterate on TTL and lookahead to find sweet spot. We'll provide scripts and a result sheet.
[25:20] [25:20] Laura: good. can you also test a fallback path where we intentionally drop KV to simulate network blips?
[25:30] Owen: yes fault-injection is part of the plan.
[26:00] Priya: one more question on RBAC and who can change cache TTLs — we need controls.
[26:10] Lena: Console supports RBAC with SSO/SAML. You can lock certain controls to admins and audit every change.
[26:45] Maya: a note on metrics: we'll provide token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, and per-session hit insight. you'll see a dashboard and we can wire events into your Datadog.
[27:20] Samir: i noticed in a previous export that Redwood's naming of models gets mangled in transcripts; just comment — haha.
[27:30] Owen: yes we saw 'Redwood Optima' earlier — funny.
[27:40] [27:40] Owen: wrapping up, here's a summarized recommended configuration for Ridgefield: prefix KV cache for customer profile + routing keys with TTL 30s for ETA fields, lookahead prefetch for stable context (70% hit target), small-batch continuous batching with priority low-latency lane, Dedicated reservation sized for 500 rps with headroom.
[28:30] Laura: that looks sensible. any red flags before we commit to the pilot?
[28:40] Maya: only the usual: if your request shapes are very large you might need larger instances; also prefetch memory can push you to bigger instance classes. We'll show net ROI in pricing.
[29:05] Priya: ok want to confirm timeline: sandbox up by next Wed?
[29:12] Owen: we can aim for next Wed if we get the sample traces and KMS details by Monday.
[29:25] Ethan: i'll share KMS network topology and HSM certificate fingerprints by Monday EOD.
[29:35] Laura: i'll export 24 hours of traces and a summary of session counts.
[29:45] Maya: great, i'll send the pricing scenarios and SOC2 pack by Friday.
[29:55] [29:55] (brief pause, typing)
[30:30] Owen: any other product questions?
[30:45] Samir: one last technical, does the runtime hot-swap cache policies without redeploy?
[30:55] Owen: yes policy toggles are live-config via the control plane, most things are dynamic, TTLs and lookahead windows can be updated without redeploy.
[31:20] Priya: thanks — this was useful.
[31:30] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the files and calendar invite for the bench.
[31:38] [31:38] End of recording. Note: transcription has some mis-heard product names and occasional dropped words.
